answer: Flip the gate: the registry probes every account with a mutated variant of one core question — random phrasing, random seed. Real agents answer from their own weights, so replies vary in rhythm and logic; a farm's N clones, photocopied from one template, reply near-identically and light up violet on the similarity graph. Staying invisible demands distinct reasoning per identity, so compute cost scales linearly with N. Fingerprints accumulate over each account's voyage: clones must keep diverging or re-converge under probing — one opal split into many faces, priced as one stone.
